An Astrophysicist studies celestial bodies, cosmic phenomena, and the physical laws governing the universe, using
telescopes, satellite data, and complex mathematical models. Cosmologists specialise further, focused on the origin,
evolution, and eventual fate of the universe as a whole — from the Big Bang to dark energy.
Indian space missions, astronomical instrumentation, and public research
Fundamental research in cosmology and astroparticle physics
International collaborations on space telescopes and missions

n Develop and test theoretical models of cosmic phenomena
n Write and publish research papers in peer-reviewed journals
n Apply for research grants and competitive observation time on telescopes
n Collaborate with international research consortia across time zones
n Present findings at conferences and participate in peer review

Deep work on theoretical modelling or data analysis code

to the latest papers on arXiv

What Is A Space Technology Engineer?

A Space Technology Engineer designs, builds, tests, and operates spacecraft, satellites, launch vehicles, and ground
systems. They work across propulsion, structures, avionics, communications, and mission operations — turning physics into
machines that survive the vacuum of space.
India's national space agency — PSLV, GSLV, Chandrayaan, Gaganyaan missions
Private Indian launch vehicle manufacturer (Vikram series)
3D-printed rocket engines and small satellite launch vehicles
Global leader in reusable launch vehicles and satellite constellations

n Write and review technical specifications and mission requirement documents

n Participate in mission readiness reviews and failure analysis
n Coordinate with cross-functional teams — propulsion, structures, avionics, software

What Is A Satellite Communication Specialist?

A Satellite Communication Specialist designs, deploys, and maintains systems that transmit voice, data, and video via
satellite links — spanning ground station antennas, transponders, modems, and network protocols. They enable everything
from DTH television to rural broadband and defence communications.

analysing rock composition, surface features, and geological history using remote sensing data, meteorite samples, and
mission data from rovers and orbiters.

n Publish findings in planetary science journals

What Is A Materials Scientist / Nanotechnologist?

A Materials Scientist or Nanotechnologist researches, designs, and engineers new materials — from semiconductors and
battery electrodes to nanocoatings and biomedical implants — by studying and manipulating their structure at the atomic
and molecular scale to achieve desired properties.
Advanced alloy and metallurgical materials research
Battery materials and energy storage R&D;
Aerospace-grade materials for spacecraft and launch vehicles

n Characterise material properties using SEM, XRD, and spectroscopy techniques
n Model material behaviour using computational simulation tools
n Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate materials into products
n Document experimental results and prepare technical reports
n Explore patentable innovations and file intellectual property

What Is A Nuclear Scientist / Engineer?

A Nuclear Scientist or Engineer researches, designs, and operates systems involving nuclear reactions — from power
reactors and fuel cycles to medical isotope production and nuclear research facilities. They work under some of the strictest
safety and regulatory frameworks of any engineering discipline.

An Oceanographer or Marine Scientist studies the physical, chemical, biological, and geological aspects of the ocean —
from currents and tides to marine life and seafloor geology — using research vessels, satellite data, and laboratory analysis
to understand and protect marine ecosystems.

geological hazards and support exploration industries.

What Is A Glaciologist / Climate Field Researcher?

A Glaciologist or Climate Field Researcher studies glaciers, ice sheets, snowpack, and permafrost to understand climate
change impacts, water resource availability, and natural hazards like glacial lake outburst floods — combining demanding
high-altitude fieldwork with satellite and laboratory analysis.

n Analyse satellite imagery to track glacier retreat over time
n Model climate change impacts on Himalayan water resources
n Assess glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) risks for downstream communities
n Publish research on cryosphere changes and climate trends
